newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rates end up on weak peso, long bond.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rates end up on weak peso, long bond.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rates pared earlier highs in late trade but still closed up 185 basis points at 23 percent on Thursday, in response to a weakening peso and gains in U.S. long bond yields, traders said.
"Inflation figures were good, but not enough to withstand pressure from the foreign exchange market," a trader said.

September consumer inflation figures, released in late trade on Wednesday, were slightly below expected at 1.60 percent. But the bellwether 48-hour peso closed three centavos weaker on Thursday, at 7.6165/7.6190 per dollar.
Traders said additional pressure on secondary rates came from the U.S. 30-year Treasury bond yield, which gained to 6.88 percent, compared to 6.80 percent during trade on Wednesday.
Traders noted that rates were under most pressure, and demand was least, in the term market.
"Term paper was trading at negative real yields, so there had to be a correction in rates," said a trader.
Rates on 28-day and 91-day Cetes both closed up 50 basis points, at 23.50 and 26.00 percent, respectively, compared with primary rates of 22.74 and 25.11.
Overnight rates on bank paper meanwhile closed up 70 basis points at 25 percent.
Banco de Mexico injected a relatively low 2.425 billion pesos into the secondary market, as liquidity pressures were eased by government spending of 1.00 billion pesos.
Total credit maturities for Friday were estimated at 6.809 billion pesos.
